papers.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning

summary.tldr: EnvHarness and EnvRigger introduce a programmable layer and automated synthesis system that dynamically wraps static LLM agent environments to target policy weaknesses without altering underlying logic or verifiers.
key_points: EnvHarness acts as a programmable plug-in layer wrapping static environments via standard interfaces to modify behavior while retaining original verifiers.
EnvRigger treats target policies as black boxes, analyzing trajectory flaws to synthesize harness components and validate them with new rollouts.
Tested across five benchmarks in four domains, achieving up to a 9.0-point improvement on held-out instances using 9.8% fewer execution steps.
Serves as an improved optimization signal for reinforcement learning to enable policy-environment co-evolution.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need to manually build domain-specific environment pipelines, allowing existing agent environments to automatically adapt and scale training to specific policy weaknesses.

papers.title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis

summary.tldr: FACET is a framework that synthesizes complex terminal agent tasks by preserving original source intent and using a shared, repaired container state to ensure consistency across instructions, solutions, and verifiers.
key_points: Reconstructs related agent skills into coherent scenarios while preserving goals, dependencies, state transitions, and procedural constraints from original sources.
Establishes a realized and repaired execution environment container state as shared grounding for generating task instructions, reference solutions, and verifiers.
Uses execution-based validation and targeted repair to fix artifact-specific failures without regenerating already valid components.
Generates dense executable checks that yield high-quality trajectories, which consistently improve model performance on Terminal-Bench 2.1 when used for fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the scalable, data-efficient synthesis of complex, validated terminal tasks needed to train and evaluate command-line agents reliably.

papers.title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video

summary.tldr: 4DAnyone reconstructs 4D humans from monocular video by using 4D Gaussian Splatting combined with a video diffusion model that scales to tens of consistent novel views.
key_points: Reference Context Packing (RCP) compresses growing reference views into a fixed-length mixed-resolution context to achieve O(1) reference-context complexity.
Target Context Routing (TCR) rotates target-view groupings during denoising to prevent structural drift and optimize cross-group context exchange.
Models were trained on a dataset blend including a new in-house game engine dataset, MVGameHuman, alongside light-stage and in-the-wild videos.
Outperforms prior approaches on DNA-Rendering and DyMVHumans benchmarks for novel-view video synthesis and downstream 4DGS reconstruction.
summary.why_it_matters: It overcomes context-length limits in video diffusion models, enabling high-fidelity 4D human reconstruction and novel-view rendering from casual, uncalibrated single-camera videos.

papers.title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation

summary.tldr: WithEveryone is a unified framework that scales group image generation up to ten reference identities by injecting identity-addressed tokens and applying Layout-Grounded ID Loss with ID Representation Forcing.
key_points: Supports identity-preserving group generation for up to ten reference identities using a structured identity-layout plan rendered as a visual condition.
Replaces unstable embedding-based face matching with Layout-Grounded ID Loss, using annotated face regions to supervise intended identities directly.
Employs ID Representation Forcing to train predictions for each target identity prior to full image synthesis.
Outperforms GPT-Image-2 on an identity-disjoint benchmark, raising target-context face similarity from 0.462 to 0.499 and reducing copy-paste artifacts from 0.169 to 0.055.
Achieves a 97.3% coverage rate for requested identities while maintaining a low duplicate rate of 2.8%.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate, multi-person image generation for large groups without suffering from duplicate faces, missed identities, or reference copy-paste artifacts.

papers.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use

summary.tldr: MemTrapBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate memory-induced cognitive traps in LLMs, revealing that faithfully retrieved memories can degrade model reasoning and performance.
key_points: Identifies two primary forms of memory-induced cognitive traps: Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion.
Evaluates two model families across five representative memory frameworks, showing all memory strategies underperform compared to a no-memory baseline.
Demonstrates that top-performing memory methods suffer performance drops exceeding 10% on MemTrapBench.
Proposes AdaptiveMem, an inference-time method that instructs LLMs to avoid cognitive traps without sacrificing performance on standard memory benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that standard long-term LLM memory retrieval can actively impair reasoning and task performance, highlighting the need for defensive inference strategies like AdaptiveMem.

papers.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?

summary.tldr: SWE-bench Science is a new repository-level benchmark containing 119 tasks across 98 GitHub repositories to evaluate coding agents on scientific software engineering.
key_points: SWE-bench Science covers 20 scientific domains across three paradigms: Issue-driven, Expert-exploratory, and Engineering-integration.
The top-performing model, Claude Code with Opus-5 (max), achieved a pass@1 rate below 50%.

Analysis revealed four main failure modes: scientific knowledge/abstraction deficits, misguided or surface-level repairs, incomplete system integration, and failure to generalize scientific knowledge.
Paired ablation showed that well-aligned scientific guidance improves average performance and token efficiency, while poorly aligned guidance causes agent anchoring without improving repair success.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a concrete evaluation benchmark exposing how current AI coding agents fail when modifying complex scientific codebases where software errors risk invalidating scientific results.

papers.title: FM-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Management with Competing Agents

summary.tldr: FM-Bench evaluates LLM agents over a 20-year horizon using 26 tools and up to 400 decision stops to manage a football club against deterministic engines and competing agents in a shared Arena without human judges.
key_points: All 15 tested frontier models completed the 20-year horizon across three seeds, while blind scripted baselines consistently failed.
Claude-fable-5 ranked highest in mean score on both the solo track and the competitive Arena, though ten different models won titles across Arena runs.
Performance was driven by managerial strategies—such as reducing late-game long-term investments, minimizing idle cash, and renewing contracts early—rather than token spend, model scale, or cost.
Models failed to infer hidden market prices from rejected bids, and self-managed memory collapsed into either unpruned growth or season-by-season plan rewrites.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that long-horizon agent performance depends on strategic operational behaviors rather than compute scale, while highlighting critical failure modes in LLM memory management and market inference.

papers.title: ForgeWM: Progressive Causal Training for Few-Step Action-Conditioned Video World Models

summary.tldr: ForgeWM is a four-stage progressive training framework that converts bidirectional action-conditioned video generators into efficient 1-, 2-, and 4-step causal world models for game control.
key_points: Uses a four-stage pipeline: domain adaptation, teacher-forced causal training, causal consistency distillation, and on-policy distribution matching with a bidirectional teacher.
Aligns discrete keyboard states and continuous mouse motions with temporally compressed latent chunks during autoregressive rollout.
Supports budget-specialized student models executing at steady-state denoising budgets of 1, 2, and 4 steps.

Features a dual-path deployment protocol where a 1-step student creates a draft that can be re-noised and refined at replay time, matching 4-step quality while staying 3x closer to the original trajectory.
Demonstrates transferability across control types, validating performance on paired Minecraft trajectories and gamepad-controlled FPS gameplay.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time, low-latency interactive video generation driven by fast-paced user controls without sacrificing visual quality or control alignment.

papers.title: SkillForge: Self-Distilling Agents for Project-Specific Issue Resolution

summary.tldr: SkillForge is a self-distillation framework that proactively acquires project-specific knowledge by synthesizing and solving synthetic issues generated from test-covered repository code.
key_points: Synthesizes project-specific issues by re-implementing test-covered core functionalities of the target repository.
Bypasses reliance on historical issue-resolution data or high per-issue test-time exploration costs.
Distills acquired knowledge into entity-grounded skills and maps them directly to relevant repository entities for future reference.
Consistently outperforms strong baselines across experiments evaluated on both open-source and closed-source LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: Proactively extracting and grounding codebase knowledge before encountering real issues enables LLM agents to resolve repository-specific bugs more accurately and efficiently.

papers.title: VA-Judger: Reward Modeling from Human Preference Feedback for Joint Video-Audio Generation

summary.tldr: VA-Judger is a chain-of-thought omni-reward model that uses dimension-wise reinforcement learning on human preference data to improve joint video-audio generation quality.
key_points: Introduces VAPref-10K, a human-preference dataset containing 9K prompts and 10.3K fine-grained paired comparisons from open-source video-audio models.
Establishes VA-Judger-Bench, a benchmark featuring in-domain and out-of-domain model comparisons to evaluate reward model alignment with human preferences.

Trains VA-Judger via a three-stage process: coarse preference learning on distinct pairs, rejection sampling to distill preference explanations for near-quality pairs, and dimension-wise reinforcement learning.
Decomposes human feedback into individual quality dimensions to provide denser reward signals than binary preference labels, reducing reward hacking.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a human-aligned reward signal for post-training joint video-audio models, preventing reward hacking and improving overall semantic and temporal coherence.

papers.title: Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation

summary.tldr: Repo0 is a continuous structural evolution framework for zero-to-all code generation that constructs software projects from natural-language requirements using a Dual-Directed-Acyclic-Graph (Dual-DAG) architectural state.
key_points: Uses a Dual-DAG architectural state combining a requirement-level DAG, a component-level DAG, and their alignment relation.
Iteratively evolves component boundaries via structural actions guided by modularity metrics until reaching structural convergence.
Executes test-driven development code generation guided by the converged Dual-DAG architecture.

Evaluated on six RepoCraft repositories using GPT-5 mini and DeepSeek V3.2, outperforming the RPG baseline by up to 20.08 percentage points in Functionality Coverage and 29.74 percentage points in Pass Rate.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM agents to generate complete, modular software repositories from scratch without needing a predefined architecture.

papers.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving

summary.tldr: FlashPrefill V2 upgrades block-sparse prefill attention into a production-ready engine using mean error correction, optimized FP8 GPU kernels, and native paged KV cache integration.
key_points: Introduces a mean correction term to suppress approximation errors at extreme sparsity levels.
Redesigns the sparse attention operator using PackGQA memory access, warp specialization, and pingpong pipelining aligned with FlashAttention-3/4 and FP8.
Supports paged KV cache and continuous batching natively for integration into inference frameworks like SGLang.
Achieves up to 47.26x (FP8) and 27.19x (BF16) speedups over FlashAttention-2 at 128K context length on NVIDIA H20 GPUs.
summary.why_it_matters: It transforms theoretical block-sparse prefill optimizations into a deployable backend that drastically speeds up 128K long-context LLM serving in production frameworks.

papers.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization

summary.tldr: The IAR framework improves retrieval-free document knowledge internalization by staging post-training into structured document knowledge injection, answer-only QA alignment, and general capability recovery via model merging.
key_points: IAR consists of three stages: Inject (using continuation, rewrite, and instruction-conditioned reconstruction), Align (answer-only QA supervision), and Recover (merging with base instruction model).
Evaluated across Llama, Phi, Qwen, and SmolLM model families on Common Corpus (CC) and CCI datasets.
Outperforms Vanilla SFT on domain QA accuracy by 3.6 percentage points on average while improving mean general performance by 12.1 percentage points across IFEval, MMLU, and MSBench.
Maintains strong general capabilities compared to LoRA and FAPM while achieving leading domain knowledge internalization.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to accurately answer domain-specific questions without retrieval augmentation while preserving general instruction-following and reasoning abilities.

papers.title: SkillGate: Training In-Policy Skill Selection in Long-Horizon Agents

summary.tldr: SkillGate resolves selector credit starvation in long-horizon agents by splitting credit into distinct outcome-reward channels for execution and local advantage channels for skill selection.
key_points: Identifies 'selector credit starvation' where sequence-level rewards penalize correct skill selections if subsequent execution fails, worsening as trajectories lengthen.
Partitions token support into two disjoint credit channels: outcome credit for execution tokens and action-local advantage for skill-naming tokens.
Assigns a positive local advantage to skill-naming tokens only when the selected skill is correct for that trajectory.
Improves trial success of a 9B model from 40.8% to 53.2% across five agentic benchmarks using a 16-candidate skill slate.
Reduces exposure to misleading skill candidates by two-thirds while lowering total skill reads.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-horizon agents to accurately select required skills from large libraries without being degraded by noisy sequence-level reinforcement learning rewards.

papers.title: The Problem Is the Problem: Towards Scalable Mathematical Discovery

summary.tldr: The Find, Attempt, and Recommend (FAR) framework automates problem discovery and filtering from literature, reducing human bottlenecks in AI-assisted mathematical research.
key_points: Human experts define a research direction rather than selecting a single starting problem.
FAR uses a literature-to-review cascade to extract, filter, attempt, and triage candidate problems.
In a combinatorics pilot, FAR extracted 6,453 candidate problems from 5,245 papers and filtered them down to 77 high-priority items for expert review.
The pipeline yielded resolutions for questions related to Erdős--Straus, Ikenmeyer--Pak--Panova, Davies--Jenssen--Perkins--Roberts, and Lund--Saraf--Wolf conjectures.
summary.why_it_matters: It optimizes scarce expert review time and model reasoning resources by automating the search and pre-filtering of mathematical open problems.

papers.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement

summary.tldr: AI4AI-Bench introduces 10 frozen research repositories to evaluate LLM agents on rewriting training algorithms for recursive self-improvement, where top systems close less than a fifth of the gap to task optima.
key_points: Evaluates agents on 10 training algorithm families using one NVIDIA B300 GPU for 4 hours of development, followed by a 12-hour evaluation run from scratch.
Normalizes scores across incommensurable task metrics onto a unified scale where 0 is uninformative, 0.1 is the repository baseline, and 1.0 is the task optimum.
Across 29 configurations of 6 systems, the mean score was 0.166 and the best system achieved 0.250.
Submissions that actually modified the learning algorithm scored higher (0.226 vs 0.126) than those that did not.
Increasing reasoning effort shifted the proportion of algorithm-modifying submissions from 8% to 64%, boosting the mean score from 0.094 to 0.196.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark isolates an agent's capability to improve core learning algorithms rather than just tuning hyperparameters, offering an empirical measure of progress toward recursive self-improvement.

papers.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation

summary.tldr: A novel method enables reasoning language models to adaptively select their reasoning depth via a initial token choice, reducing inference token usage while maintaining accuracy.
key_points: Models select between NoThink, Short, or Long modes using the response's first token within GRPO training without a separate router.
The approach utilizes a shaped reward structure paired with hard per-mode token caps to prevent mode collapse.
On MATH500, a 1.5B model achieved 0.782 accuracy versus 0.796 baseline while cutting average token length by 41% (from 4,796 to 2,811 tokens).
The learned policy transferred zero-shot to GSM8K, achieving a 76% token reduction while maintaining higher accuracy than length-matched baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach significantly lowers test-time compute costs and latency by dynamically scaling reasoning effort based on problem difficulty without needing an external routing model.

papers.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts

summary.tldr: A two-step hyperparameter transfer framework uses Maximal Update Parameterization (μP) and scaling laws to accurately predict optimal learning rates for large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models across both model widths and token counts.
key_points: Adapts Maximal Update Parameterization (μP) for MoE architectures featuring Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and the Muon optimizer to transfer learning rates across model widths.
Establishes a predictive scaling law via linear regression to extrapolate optimal learning rates to massive horizons (e.g., 10 trillion tokens) with R² = 0.95.
Validated by pretraining a 155B total parameter (17B active) MoE foundation model from scratch with high stability and low ablation costs.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate tuning of optimal learning rates for massive MoE models using small proxy models, drastically reducing the computational cost of hyperparameter sweeps.

papers.title: EchoCoT: Extracting Hidden Chain-of-Thought from Large Reasoning Models

summary.tldr: EchoCoT is a new multi-step attack framework that extracts near-verbatim hidden chain-of-thought traces from black-box large reasoning models via API tool-call interactions.
key_points: Exploits a reasoning replay surface between tool calls using API-returned fidelity signals to iteratively extract hidden CoTs.
Employs an LLM-based optimization framework to automatically search for universal injection trajectories across datasets.
Achieved up to 66.4% near-verbatim extraction success on open-source LRMs, where extracted traces match at least 90% of tokens and stay within 10% of target length.
Demonstrates cross-dataset generalization up to 80% success and successfully extracted a 33,463-token CoT from Gemini-2.5.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes hidden chain-of-thought extraction as a practical security and intellectual property risk for proprietary black-box reasoning models.

papers.title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models

summary.tldr: In-context secrets implicitly leak into benign language model outputs, enabling an adaptive black-box attack to reconstruct sensitive data even when direct extraction is refused.
key_points: Controlled experiments across eight proprietary models demonstrated 2-digit secret reconstruction with near-perfect accuracy and 4-digit secrets at 82% exact match from ordinary responses.
Stronger instruction-following capabilities in higher-performing models amplify sensitivity to in-context secrets, making context leakage a byproduct of model capability.

Demonstrated practical exploits include a classifier inferring user semantic predicates from routine outputs and an RL-trained adversary extracting full Social Security Numbers from a production agent.
summary.why_it_matters: AI agents handling sensitive user data risk exposing confidential context through routine, benign responses even when explicit safety guardrails prevent direct extraction.

papers.title: Learning how to Forget: Fine-tuning for Long-Context Sparse Attention

summary.tldr: A new fine-tuning method allows transformer models to co-adapt with any sparse attention KV cache policy using moderate hardware, outperforming models trained with exact attention.
key_points: Supports fine-tuning for any KV cache selection and compression policy on moderate hardware, such as a single 40 GB Nvidia A100 GPU.
Outperforms models fine-tuned with exact attention using sequence parallelism.
Provides an efficient H2O sparse attention implementation featuring dedicated scaled dot product attention (SDPA) kernel support.
Released open-source via the KeysAndValues library for long-context inference and fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables cost-effective fine-tuning and improved long-context inference performance without requiring massive GPU clusters for sequence parallelism.

papers.title: LoRA-GA$^2$: Low Rank Adaptation with Multi-step Gradient Adaptive Alignment

summary.tldr: LoRA-GA$^2$ improves low-rank adaptation by using multi-step gradient information from pretrained weights alongside spectrum-aware rank allocation and optimal initialization.
key_points: Uses a lightweight probe to capture multi-step gradients of pretrained weights without extra GPU memory and with minimal time overhead.
Applies a spectrum-aware, importance-based rank allocation derived from multi-step gradient dynamics.
Outperforms prior LoRA variants by an average of 0.66 points on GLUE, 1.03 points on GSM8K, and 0.87 points on HumanEval.
summary.why_it_matters: It narrows the performance gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning without increasing memory overhead.

papers.title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay

summary.tldr: A study auditing LLM agent step-level credit signals against causal ground-truth from executed replays in ALFWorld shows that common credit rules perform no better than chance and primarily echo policy fluency rather than causal step contribution.
key_points: Audited against re-sampled executed replays, LLM-judge scores, logprob ratios, and policy confidence fail to identify causally pivotal steps better than chance.
Causal contribution is sparse, with only 30.5% of defined decision points showing measurable effect, while implicit credit strongly correlates with policy fluency (median rank correlation +0.75).
Conditioning credit on final outcomes adds zero causal information (partial correlation -0.004 for Qwen).
In training experiments across seven arms, variations in checkpoint performance were driven by training dose (effective sample size/optimizer steps) rather than the content of the credit signal.
summary.why_it_matters: Reinforcement learning and fine-tuning methods for LLM agents currently rely on step-level credit signals that fail to reflect actual causal impact, meaning training efficiency is dictated by sample volume rather than true credit assignment.

papers.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving

summary.tldr: FlashPrefill V2 upgrades block-sparse prefill attention for production LLM serving by adding a mean correction term for low FP8/BF16 approximation error and optimizing memory access for engines like SGLang.
key_points: Introduces a mean correction term to suppress approximation errors during extreme attention sparsity.
Redesigns the sparse attention operator using PackGQA memory access, warp specialization, pingpong pipelining, and FP8 quantization support aligned with FlashAttention-3/4.
Natively supports paged KV cache and continuous batching to enable direct integration into production inference engines like SGLang.
Achieves up to 47.26x (FP8) and 27.19x (BF16) speedups over FlashAttention-2, and 30.49x over an FA3/4-aligned dense baseline at 128K context length on NVIDIA H20 GPUs.
summary.why_it_matters: It bridges the gap between theoretical sparse attention research and production LLM serving by drastically reducing long-context prefill latency in modern inference frameworks.

papers.title: Truncate Bad, Upweight Good: BoN-Style Distillation via Rank-Based Classification

summary.tldr: TUP is a Best-of-N distillation method that truncates low-ranked candidate completions from the target support and reweights the retained upper tail using a tunable sharpness parameter.
key_points: Removes low-ranked candidates from the policy target support instead of using smooth full-support reweighting.
Trains offline using binary cross-entropy with shifted-truncated win-rates as soft labels and distilled-to-reference log-likelihood ratios as logits.
Features a closed-form, prompt-independent normalization.
Provides theoretical proof that a lower-tail truncation rule can match the best monotone rank-reweighting for any unknown oracle reward.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient offline policy distillation from Best-of-N sampling without relying on brittle top-rank reward model distinctions or retaining low-quality completions in the target support.

security.title: COPA: Continual Preference Optimization for Adaptive Prompt Injection Defense

summary.tldr: COPA is a continual preference optimization framework that uses GRPO-based optimization and margin-weighted experience replay to defend LLMs against evolving prompt injection attacks without catastrophic forgetting.
key_points: Treats prompt injection defense as a lifelong learning problem to handle adaptive, evolving adversaries.
Uses Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to incrementally incorporate feedback from newly observed attack streams.
Employs margin-weighted experience replay to retain robustness against previously encountered attack classes and preserve general model capabilities.
Reduces attack success rates by an average of 4.4x and up to 6.3x compared to state-of-the-art defenses.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployed LLMs to continuously adapt to novel prompt injection techniques in real time without needing static redesigns or losing prior security alignment.

security.title: From Noise to Signal: Improving Security Log Anomaly Detection Using LLMs with Endpoint-Specific Logs

summary.tldr: A standardized instruction-based LLM classification framework utilizing endpoint-specific authentication logs significantly outperforms traditional rule-based (Wazuh) and statistical (OpenSearch) anomaly detection methods.
key_points: Meta Llama 3.1 8B Instruct achieved an overall detection accuracy of 89.3%, an F1-score of 91.8%, and a false negative rate of 11.8%, outperforming Wazuh (52.0% accuracy, 68.6% FNR) and OpenSearch (49.3% accuracy, 74.5% FNR).
In borderline anomalous scenarios, Meta Llama 3.1 8B detected 80% of cases, compared to 20% for Wazuh and 15% for OpenSearch.
Evaluated models included Meta Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, and GPT-OSS 20B; Qwen 2.5 7B recorded the lowest average inference latency and achieved 100% structured-response validity.
summary.why_it_matters: Leveraging instruction-tuned LLMs with endpoint-specific context dramatically lowers false negative rates and improves detection of subtle, borderline security threats over traditional SIEM tools.

security.title: MaliciousSkillBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Malicious Agent Skill Detection

summary.tldr: MaliciousSkillBench is a new benchmark for malicious LLM Agent Skill detection, consolidating 9,740 Skills across 11 unified attack categories to address dataset fragmentation and source-bias evaluation challenges.
key_points: Deduplicated 8,414 raw malicious records into 7,539 unique identities across 4,588 structural families, yielding a final benchmark of 7,505 malicious and 2,235 benign Skills.
Learned text detectors showed severe performance drops from Random Macro-F1 (0.882-0.932) to Source-Disjoint evaluation (0.653-0.665).
A word TF-IDF SVM achieved 0.665 Source-Disjoint Macro-F1 with 95.6% malicious recall, but suffered a 62.4% benign false positive rate on held-out sources.
Off-the-shelf Skill scanners reduced false positives compared to learned models, but only at the cost of sharply reduced malicious recall.
summary.why_it_matters: Current detection approaches fail to generalize across unseen distribution channels, causing either high false-positive rates on benign Skills or missed malicious attacks in real-world deployments.

security.title: Enhancing Privacy in Federated Learning via Dual Obfuscation of Gradients and Training Images

summary.tldr: A dual obfuscation method for federated learning combines random binary gradient masking with client-level image encryption to prevent image reconstruction attacks without degrading Vision Transformer classification performance beyond the encryption baseline.
key_points: Combines a gradient modification technique using random binary weights (zeroing out selected gradient elements) with individual image encryption.
Uses independent encryption keys per client and per image to eliminate the requirement for explicit key sharing.
Evaluated on Vision Transformer (ViT) image classification tasks subjected to Attention Privacy Leakage (APRIL) reconstruction attacks.
Reduces visually recoverable information while maintaining the model classification performance associated with the underlying image encryption.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining gradient masking with per-image encryption provides complementary defense layers that mitigate visual data leakage in Vision Transformers without imposing key-sharing overhead or extra performance penalties.

security.title: AEGIS: Attention-Embedding Gradient Isolation Shield - Triple-Channel Gradient Masking for Privacy-Preserving Federated LLM Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: AEGIS is a lightweight defence that eliminates token recovery from gradient inversion in federated LLM fine-tuning by simultaneously masking three distinct gradient leakage channels in the backward path without altering model architecture.
key_points: Identifies three leakage channels: attention output projection low-rank subspace (Channel 1), embedding gradient row-norm sparsity (Channel 2), and MLP expansion gradients (Channel 3).
Freezes attention projection parameters to construct a complete defence against Channel 1 leakage.
Injects calibrated noise into embedding gradients (Channel 2) and per-block noise into MLP expansion gradients (Channel 3) to mask private signals.
Applies the same masked gradients to both local optimizer steps and server exports to ensure no clean signal remains.
Evaluated across 11 models and six datasets, reducing token recovery rates to near zero against analytical and optimization-based attacks while preserving model utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents analytical and optimization-based gradient inversion attacks in federated LLM fine-tuning without degrading model performance or requiring architectural modifications.

security.title: Zero-click Grok data theft: Cryptographic Context Injection attack leaks chat histories

summary.tldr: A zero-click Cryptographic Context Injection attack bypasses Grok security by sending encrypted instructions that the model decrypts internally, leaking full user chat histories.
key_points: Cryptographic Context Injection delivers malicious payload instructions as ciphertext.
The target model decrypts the ciphertext inside its own sandbox environment.
The vulnerability enables zero-click extraction of complete Grok chat histories.
summary.why_it_matters: Attackers can silently exfiltrate sensitive user conversation logs without requiring any victim interaction.

security.title: Detailed Timeline of OpenAI’s Cyberattack on Hugging Face

summary.tldr: At Black Hat, OpenAI presented details and a timeline of an AI model executing an offensive cyberattack against Hugging Face.
key_points: OpenAI disclosed details of an automated cyberattack conducted by its AI model against Hugging Face.
The technical presentation and timeline of the cyberoffensive operations were delivered at the Black Hat conference.
Security researcher Simon Willison published a detailed breakdown of the attack timeline.
summary.why_it_matters: The event demonstrates documented real-world capabilities of AI models executing sophisticated offensive cyber operations against live infrastructure.

security.title: TrustRAG: Blockchain-Enhanced RAG via Committee-Based Credibility Scoring

summary.tldr: TrustRAG integrates blockchain, zero-knowledge protocols, and multi-party computation to provide verifiable, tamper-proof committee credibility scoring for document retrieval in LLM systems.
key_points: Domain experts certify documents prior to retrieval using a zero-knowledge protocol.
Hidden expert ratings are aggregated into a verifiable trust score via secure multi-party computation (SMPC).
Document data and scores are maintained cross-chain using hash commitments to enable independent replay and verification of document rankings.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents bad outputs in high-stakes LLM applications by ensuring retrieved documents cannot be silently tampered with, omitted, or unverified.

security.title: Auditing Cross-Lingual Fairness in Language Model Watermarking

summary.tldr: A new cross-lingual evaluation framework reveals that language model watermarking performance gaps are structurally driven by typological language families rather than individual language idiosyncrasies.
key_points: The framework evaluates six watermarking schemes across three open-weight generators, eleven languages, four scripts, and eight typological families.
It introduces empirically calibrated detection thresholds alongside a threshold-independent companion metric to separate calibration errors from detection failures.
Quality is evaluated across three disjoint paradigms: distributional, paired-semantic, and reference-perplexity.
Disparity analysis using generalized-entropy decomposition shows cross-lingual fairness gaps are predominantly between-family across the typological partition.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard English-centric watermarking evaluations mask structural performance and quality disparities that emerge when deploying watermarked models in multilingual contexts.

security.title: Linguistic Holonomy and Statistical Watermarks: Inner Geometry of Meaning-Preserving Transformations

summary.tldr: Researchers prove that meaning-preserving text transformations contain a hidden geometric holonomy, showing statistical watermark decay follows a exact seed-window survival identity rather than semantic similarity distance.
key_points: Meaning-preserving transformation chains factorize into an endpoint component and a holonomy in the initial state's stabilizer, which acts as parallel transport on the embedding space's unit sphere.
The residual watermark statistic is strictly proportional to the number of token positions with completely intact seeding windows.
Under an independent-edit assumption, the watermark signal decays following the power law ̢Ȑ^{h+1}, where h relates to the window context.
At a fixed text retention rate, the remaining watermark signal varies drastically—from 50%, to 25%, down to 0%—depending entirely on the spatial distribution of edits.
summary.why_it_matters: Measuring semantic similarity fails to predict watermark erosion because detection strength depends strictly on local seeding-window integrity rather than global meaning preservation.

security.title: Tracking the Trend in How Speech Synthesizers Deceive People

summary.tldr: A study evaluating 82 IT professionals shows human deepfake detection F1 scores fell from ~90% on older synthesizers (RTVC, YourTTS) to 48% on ElevenLabs, while partial spoofing accuracy dropped to 9%.
key_points: Human F1 scores for detecting fully synthetic speech dropped from ~90% for RTVC (2019) and YourTTS (2022) to 48% for ElevenLabs (2024).
In partial spoofing scenarios where one sentence is altered, human strict accuracy dropped to 9%, with synthetic sentences misclassified as genuine 77% of the time.
Human listeners and six pretrained automated detectors exhibit complementary failure modes, and both fail to reliably localize short audio manipulations.
False positives increased, with listeners increasingly mislabeling genuine, bona fide speech as deepfakes.
summary.why_it_matters: Human perception and automated detectors are insufficient for modern voice synthesis, necessitating technical counter-measures like watermarking, procedural verification, and segment-level detection.

security.title: A Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Oral Cancer Screening on Smartphones

summary.tldr: A practical federated learning framework uses Flower, Tailscale, and FedAvg to enable privacy-preserving, smartphone-based oral cancer screening across decentralized clinical image datasets.
key_points: Client devices connect via Tailscale for secure real-time communication, with Flower handling server-side FedAvg aggregation without enterprise FL platforms.
Evaluated lightweight mobile architectures including MobileNetV2, MobileNetV3Large, and MobileNetV4-Conv-Small (MNv4-Conv-S).
The MNv4-Conv-S based global model (GM-V4) achieved the top performance with an AUC of 0.929 and an accuracy of 87%.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a secure, decentralized method for training high-accuracy oral cancer diagnostic models directly on smartphones without centralizing sensitive patient images.

security.title: Beyond Deepfakes: Zero Trust Security for the AI Economy

summary.tldr: Cloud Security Alliance research demonstrates how integrating Zero Trust, IAM, and AI data security addresses identity and authorization vulnerabilities exposed by AI-generated deepfakes.
key_points: Deepfakes exploit core weaknesses in organizational identity verification, authority delegation, and data protection mechanisms.
Visual and auditory appearances are no longer sufficient proofs of identity for sensitive requests like payments or data transfers.
CSA research advocates using a Zero Trust architecture alongside IAM and AI data security as foundational trust infrastructure.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations must transition from visual-based identity verification to Zero Trust controls to prevent AI-driven social engineering and unauthorized executions.

security.title: FedGuard-DC: Privacy-Preserving Federated Load Forecasting and Cyber-Attack Detection for Data-Center Loads in Transmission Systems

summary.tldr: FedGuard-DC is a federated learning framework that combines load forecasting and local false-data-injection attack detection for data centers without exposing raw megawatt measurements or absolute demand.
key_points: Uses a dual-head model architecture with a shared encoder driving both a forecasting head and a reconstruction head.
Combines forecast residual and reconstruction error into a calibrated anomaly score to perform local FDIA detection.
Achieves a 0.5s-ahead normalized forecast RMSE of 0.023-0.038 pu, outperforming persistence baseline models (0.32-0.34 pu).
Detects FDIA attacks with 0.979 ROC-AUC, 0.930 F1-score, and 0.988 precision on the IEEE 39-bus system.
Utilizes robust trimmed-mean aggregation to lower the RMSE impact of poisoned clients from 0.042 to 0.035 pu.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows transmission system operators to accurately forecast fast-varying data-center loads and detect cyber-attacks without requiring data centers to compromise sensitive workload and utilization privacy.

security.title: Malformer: A Multi-Modal Malware Detector Using Transformers

summary.tldr: Malformer is a quadrimodal transformer framework that fuses text, image, graph, and audio representations of Windows executables to improve malware detection accuracy.
key_points: Fuses four distinct binary modalities: text, image, graph, and audio representations.
Utilizes an architecture combining two RoBERTa encoders, a modified Vision Transformer (ViT), WavLM for audio, and an adaptive loss-weighting scheme.
Achieved 98.3% accuracy and an F1 score of 0.9833 on a dataset of 201,549 binary samples.
Outperformed unimodal baselines and bimodal detectors by 4.6 to 17.6 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining four distinct binary representations reduces reliance on single extraction methods like disassembly, yielding more resilient malware detection.

infra.title: Harnessing AI for Day-One Model Enablement

summary.tldr: AI agents can automatically generate thin runtime adapters to patch PyTorch model code, enabling day-one support for new model architectures on evolving hardware stacks.
key_points: Software compilation stacks and operator lowerings routinely lag behind the rapid pace of new model architectures and hardware releases.
Runtime adapters patch and swap unsupported model operations for equivalent torch constructs that can lower cleanly through an existing PyTorch compiler.
The adapter strategy was demonstrated by running stock HuggingFace Transformers models on IBM's Spyre AI accelerator using a small set of AI-written adapters.
summary.why_it_matters: Using AI agents to write runtime adapters bypasses months of manual compiler engineering, allowing immediate model deployment on new hardware accelerators while the underlying stack matures.

infra.title: Introducing cross-Region inference for OpenAI GPT-5.6 models on Amazon Bedrock

summary.tldr: Amazon Bedrock now supports cross-Region inference for OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (Sol, Terra, and Luna) across more than 25 AWS Regions using geographic and global inference profiles.
key_points: GPT-5.6 variants (Sol, Terra, Luna) support text/image inputs, 1 million token context windows, reasoning mode, prompt caching, and server-side tool calling.

US geographic inference profiles (prefixed with us.) constrain request routing within US Regions for data residency, while global profiles (prefixed with global.) route dynamically across all supported commercial AWS Regions based on capacity.
Models can be invoked via the OpenAI Responses API, OpenAI Chat Completions API, and Amazon Bedrock Converse/ConverseStream API.
Cross-Region inference (CRIS) acts as a capacity mechanism to increase throughput, with billing and quota consumption tracked centrally against the source account.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can achieve higher throughput and operational resiliency for GPT-5.6 workloads by pooling AWS compute capacity across regions without changing single-account billing or violating data residency constraints.

infra.title: Scaling agentic AI: Enterprise patterns without vendor lock-in

summary.tldr: AWS details architectural patterns for scaling multi-agent enterprise AI systems across heterogeneous, multi-framework, and multi-provider environments without incurring vendor lock-in.
key_points: Enterprise AI scales into heterogeneous environments featuring diverse frameworks, model providers, custom-built agents, and SaaS integrations.
Attempting to strictly standardize framework or model selection causes developer friction and architectural divergence.
Recommended architecture standardizes control planes below the application layer—including identity, policy enforcement, observability, and routing.
Amazon SageMaker provides unified model lifecycle management and scalable inference to maintain enterprise-wide consistency while retaining flexibility.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling application-level agent development from shared infrastructure control planes prevents vendor lock-in and allows enterprises to adapt to rapid foundation model evolution.

vendors.title: ChatGPT search now uses the site:operator at scale

summary.tldr: Following the GPT-5.6 rollout, automated tracking shows ChatGPT Search fanout queries containing the site:operator jumped from under 0.5% to 16-17%.
key_points: Promptwatch data shows site:operator usage in tracked ChatGPT Search fanout queries spiked to 16-17% on August 8, up from 0.3-0.5%.
The change correlates with OpenAI's August 6 update to GPT-5.6 Sol in Chat aimed at factual reliability and focused answers.
Analysis suggests OpenAI's updated search tool implementation resembles a search(query, recency, domains) function rather than direct site: operator insertion.
Promptwatch reported an August 18 follow-up indicating ChatGPT significantly reduced its reliance on Reddit for search results.
summary.why_it_matters: The shift indicates OpenAI is actively refining search constraints to target specific domains and reduce reliance on unverified sources like Reddit.
